features.ip_note: Residential IPs with auto-rotation on by default (190+ countries); bandwidth metered at 25,000 credits/GB on every plan (~$10.6/GB at Build B1 credit value), no $/GB published; no BYO proxy documented.

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.

No guaranteed vCPU allocation published; browser-hour is not a verified 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM equivalent. The sizes card keeps unknown hardware null; do not coerce it to zero or auto-rank against resource-guaranteed VMs.
Browser RAM is not published unless a specific mode overrides it.
All products share a credit balance; do not count separate fetch, proxy and session allowances. 404/410 are billable successes.

Top-up equivalent hourly rate in card is marginal only while packs are available. Engine cannot enforce four-pack cap, monthly rollover, request-specific response-size limits or per-plan network rates.
Browser TTL at most 15 min: 8 h uninterrupted sessions infeasible. Requires checkpoint/auth restoration and at least 32 segments per eight-hour shift.
GPU/guest OS/CPU/RAM, arbitrary snapshots, replay-storage fees and a separate CAPTCHA fee are unpublished.

Browser Sessions also bill bandwidth at 25,000 credits/GB (= the credits of ~83 browser-hours per GB): about $14.77/GB at the Build B1 top-up value down to $2.78/GB at Scale S3. network.egress_gib stays null because the dollar value depends on the plan rung, so bandwidth-heavy workloads are underestimated.

fleet.tiers: Free 5; Build 20; Launch 50; Growth 100; Scale 200; Enterprise 400–1,000+ custom.
fleet.notes: Concurrency shared across products/interfaces, not a separate allowance per API key or browser product. 10 fits Build, 50 Launch, 300/1,000 Enterprise.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: after the time expires, the session closes automatically, freeing up resources and ensuring clean session management
snapshot_auto.note: Ephemeral CDP browser sessions, TTL 1-15 min; nothing documented about saving/restoring session state on close.

harness_api.quote: Connect Playwright or Puppeteer directly to the Browser Sessions API
harness_api.note: Remote browser only, driven via CDP (Puppeteer/Playwright) or the ZenRows MCP browser tools; no code-execution sandbox in which an agent harness could run.

guest_firewall.quote: The Zenrows Browser Sessions uses the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) as its communication standard.
guest_firewall.note: No shell/root inside the browser host; only CDP access, and some browser-modifying commands are blocked.

image_oci.quote: Zenrows is web data infrastructure built for agents and applications. It gives them reliable access to the live web ... It exposes a small set of primitives: Fetch, Extract, Batch, and Browser Sessions.
image_oci.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Zenrows only exposes managed browser/HTTP endpoints, not a machine you can boot from a custom image.

docker_inside.quote: It exposes a small set of primitives: Fetch, Extract, Batch, and Browser Sessions.
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — there is no general-purpose compute/container runtime, only a remote browser reached via CDP.

nested_virt.quote: The Zenrows Browser Sessions uses the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) as its communication standard.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — only CDP access to a managed browser tab, no shell/root access to run VMs.

desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — access is via CDP WebSocket for automation, not a VNC/RDP graphical desktop stream.

ssh.quote: The Zenrows Browser Sessions uses the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) as its communication standard.
ssh.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no shell access to the underlying host, only CDP to the browser.

snapshot.quote: after the time expires, the session closes automatically, freeing up resources and ensuring clean session management
snapshot.note: Sessions are ephemeral (TTL 1-15 min) with no documented disk or memory snapshot/restore capability.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: after the time expires, the session closes automatically, freeing up resources and ensuring clean session management
snapshot_on_demand.note: No API/CLI checkpoint or snapshot mechanism documented for Browser Sessions.

fork.quote: It exposes a small set of primitives: Fetch, Extract, Batch, and Browser Sessions.
fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no concept of cloning a running machine/session.

fork_running.quote: It exposes a small set of primitives: Fetch, Extract, Batch, and Browser Sessions.
fork_running.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: It exposes a small set of primitives: Fetch, Extract, Batch, and Browser Sessions.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

pause_resume.quote: after the time expires, the session closes automatically, freeing up resources and ensuring clean session management
pause_resume.note: Sessions run to a TTL and close; no pause/resume of a running browser session is documented.

wake_on_request.quote: Zenrows' Browser Sessions ... offering 99.9% uptime for uninterrupted scraping.
wake_on_request.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — each request/session is spun up fresh, there is no stopped machine that 'wakes' on a request.

persistent_disk.quote: after the time expires, the session closes automatically, freeing up resources and ensuring clean session management
persistent_disk.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — ephemeral browser sessions with no persistent filesystem across sessions documented.

volume_attach.quote: It exposes a small set of primitives: Fetch, Extract, Batch, and Browser Sessions.
volume_attach.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no volume/storage attachment concept for a managed browser API.

volume_shared.quote: It exposes a small set of primitives: Fetch, Extract, Batch, and Browser Sessions.
volume_shared.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

auto_stop_idle.quote: after the time expires, the session closes automatically, freeing up resources and ensuring clean session management
auto_stop_idle.note: Every browser session automatically closes/frees resources at its TTL (1-15 min), the functional equivalent of an idle/timeout auto-stop.

live_resize.quote: It exposes a small set of primitives: Fetch, Extract, Batch, and Browser Sessions.
live_resize.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no CPU/RAM sizing is exposed to change on a running session.

agent_harnesses.quote: MCP, Skills, Templates, Workflows, Recipes, and Evals: the pieces that make Zenrows installable and usable by an AI agent, not just callable by one.
agent_harnesses.note: Zenrows ships an agent toolkit/MCP server for coding agents to call it as a tool, but it does not offer a sandbox with coding-agent harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) preinstalled inside it.

own_agent_api.quote: Give any MCP-compatible AI tool, agent, or application real-time access to the live web. One integration combines fast scraping and full browser automation, with anti-bot bypass on every tool.
own_agent_api.note: Zenrows provides tools (Fetch/Extract/Browser Sessions) for other agents to call; it does not run/host its own autonomous browser-use or research agent that customers drive via a first-party task-agent API.

lang_python.quote: Official Zenrows Python SDK for Fetch. Handles authentication, retries, and concurrency so you can scrape with less boilerplate.
lang_python.note: First-party Python SDK for Fetch/Batch; Browser Sessions also documented with Pyppeteer/Playwright Python integration.

lang_node.quote: Official Zenrows Node.js SDK for Fetch. Handles authentication, retries, and concurrency so you can scrape with less boilerplate.
lang_node.note: First-party Node.js SDK for Fetch/Batch; Browser Sessions documented with Puppeteer/Playwright Node.js integration.

public_ipv4.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — customers connect to a shared Zenrows endpoint over WSS; there is no dedicated public IPv4 assigned per customer machine.

inbound_https.quote: It exposes a small set of primitives: Fetch, Extract, Batch, and Browser Sessions.
inbound_https.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — there is no customer-exposed port/service on the browser host reachable via a provider-issued HTTPS URL.

ingress_rules.quote: It exposes a small set of primitives: Fetch, Extract, Batch, and Browser Sessions.
ingress_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no inbound ports/services to apply provider-side access rules to.

egress_allowlist.quote: IP Auto-Rotation: Rotate IPs with every request to avoid bans and blocks, ensuring your scraping remains undetected.
egress_allowlist.note: Zenrows' proxy network exists to reach arbitrary target sites (the opposite of restricting egress); no outbound allow/deny-list or no-internet mode is documented.

egress_http_rules.quote: IP Auto-Rotation: Rotate IPs with every request to avoid bans and blocks, ensuring your scraping remains undetected.
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no method/path-level egress rule controls documented.

secret_proxy.quote: apikey required string ... Your unique API key for authentication
secret_proxy.note: Auth is via a Zenrows API key on requests; no documented first-party credential-injection proxy for third-party HTTP APIs or model-provider keys inside sessions.

static_egress_ip.quote: IP Auto-Rotation: Rotate IPs with every request to avoid bans and blocks, ensuring your scraping remains undetected.
static_egress_ip.note: The product's design is IP rotation (over 55 million residential IPs, rotating by default), the opposite of a fixed outbound IP; no static IP option documented.

gpu.quote: It exposes a small set of primitives: Fetch, Extract, Batch, and Browser Sessions.
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — a managed browser/scraping API has no GPU compute offering.

windows.quote: It exposes a small set of primitives: Fetch, Extract, Batch, and Browser Sessions.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no selectable guest OS/machine type is exposed at all, let alone Windows.

macos.quote: It exposes a small set of primitives: Fetch, Extract, Batch, and Browser Sessions.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

arm64.quote: It exposes a small set of primitives: Fetch, Extract, Batch, and Browser Sessions.
arm64.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no selectable machine architecture is exposed to customers.

self_host.quote: Zenrows is web data infrastructure built for agents and applications.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Zenrows is a hosted SaaS API; no self-hosted deployment package is documented.

byoc.quote: Zenrows is web data infrastructure built for agents and applications.
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no bring-your-own-cloud managed deployment is documented; service runs solely on Zenrows' own infrastructure.

open_source.quote: Zenrows is web data infrastructure built for agents and applications.
open_source.note: Zenrows is a commercial SaaS product; the core scraping/browser infrastructure is closed-source (only client SDKs/CLI are open on GitHub, not the core service).

isolation.quote: The Zenrows Browser Sessions uses the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) as its communication standard.
isolation.note: derived: Browser Sessions is a remote, fully-managed headless-Chrome-over-CDP product with no shell/root/VM access exposed (viewport, user agent and other browser-modifying commands are blocked); no VM/microVM/isolate tech is documented, consistent with a containerized per-session Chrome instance rather than a dedicated VM per customer.

hipaa.note: The Zenrows Trust Center lists only ISO 27001:2022 and SOC 2 under Compliance; HIPAA/BAA is not mentioned anywhere on the trust center, security, or GDPR pages.

eu_data_residency.quote: Zenrows is primarily hosted on Digital Ocean, a cloud hosting service. We regularly audit our practices against Digital Ocean's recommended security guidelines for data protection.
eu_data_residency.note: Zenrows (the company) is EU-based (Spain) and GDPR-compliant, but no page offers a customer-selectable EU-only hosting/data-residency region for Browser Sessions infrastructure or account data; the only 'region' setting documented (proxy_region=eu) selects the residential-proxy exit IP location, not where the session/browser or data is processed or stored.

usage_api.quote: The Billing page is where you manage everything related to paying for Zenrows: your subscription, extra credits (top-ups), and your record of past payments and invoices. Open it from the Billing entry in the dashboard sidebar.
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; cost: no; Usage and cost viewing is restricted to the web dashboard (Billing page) and email alerts; no REST API endpoint is documented for retrieving billable usage metrics per session, per tag, or per resource.

locations_quote: Zenrows is primarily hosted on Digital Ocean, a cloud hosting service. We regularly audit our practices against Digital Ocean's recommended security guidelines for data protection.
